llm.summary: The skill is a coherent self-hosted speech-service guide that clearly discloses its network, shell, voice-cloning, and server-side storage risks.

dimensions.detail: Network access, curl/ffmpeg/docker examples, large model downloads, GPU use, and server-side URL fetching are proportionate to the speech-service purpose, with documented limits and deployment warnings.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses normal Docker run commands for CPU/CUDA images and a host data volume; this is expected for a self-hosted ML service but users should review the image and bind the port appropriately.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill tells agents and users to send audio, text, URLs, and optional voice samples to the configured TALKIES_URL, but it repeatedly warns that data leaves the host and should only go to trusted instances.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Server-side staged files, cached URL downloads, custom voice files, and model weights persist under the configured data directory; the artifact discloses cleanup, auth, shared-bucket, and retention limitations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The ASR/TTS, voice discovery, transcription, synthesis, staging, MCP, and Docker setup instructions all match the stated purpose of operating a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible speech service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to run or use a trusted talkies server. Keep TALKIES_URL pointed at localhost or a server you control, enable TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN for any shared or exposed deployment, prefer HTTPS off-host, avoid sending confidential text/audio or voice samples to untrusted operators, and clean up staged files or cached URL downloads when finished.
llm.findings:
[E1] expected: The flagged TTS examples transmit input text to TALKIES_URL, which is necessary for remote/self-hosted synthesis and is explicitly disclosed as data egress to a trusted operator-chosen server.
[E1] expected: The flagged cloned-voice workflow sends selected reference voice material through the configured service, but the artifact describes this as the intended voice-cloning mode and includes consent and trust-boundary warnings.
[E1] expected: The repeated speech-synthesis workflow again reflects the core TTS function; the risk is real for sensitive text but is documented rather than hidden or purpose-mismatched.
